Subject: Audit logs & data access — follow-up and sample request

Hi Sarah — great to meet you and the FinCo team on today's call. Quick recap and the asks we discussed so everything's captured: 

- Recap: We covered Redwood's serving model, how we surface audit logs for data access, and options for retention/residency.
- Your compliance asks: (1) sample audit log export (CSV/JSON schema), (2) confirmation of which fields are recorded (who, what, when, source IP, request id), (3) retention options and proof of residency, and (4) redaction/pseudonymization options for PII.

Next steps / asks from you: please confirm the desired export format (CSV vs JSON lines), the required retention window for this scope (e.g., 1 year, 7 years), and whether your auditors need a signed attestation or a sample data export is sufficient for initial qualification. Also let me know if the compliance contact (I've copied Marissa) should be the primary recipient for the sample.

We'll assemble a sanitized sample export and a short technical note that lists the fields and retention behaviors. Ben (cc'd offline) will pull the export and Marissa will handle the compliance summary.

Thanks — I'll follow up with the sample by EOD Tue once we have the retention confirmed.

--

From: Sarah Nguyen <sarah.nguyen@fincobank.com>

Subject: Re: Audit logs & data access — follow-up and sample request

Thanks Jordan — appreciate the recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) For the sample, we prefer CSV and a short JSON schema if possible.
2) Fields that are mandatory for our auditors: timestamp (UTC), actor identity (user id or service principal), API key id (or token id), request id, affected resource id, operation type (read/write/export), and source IP.
3) Retention: initial ask is for a 7-year retention policy for audit logs (banking requirement); please indicate whether that's supported in hosted vs dedicated/private deployments and any associated costs.
4) Residency: logs must be stored within US regions (we can specify preferred regions later).
5) PII handling: auditors will need a short note on redaction/pseudonymization options and whether raw payloads (request/response bodies) are retained in logs by default.

For the sample, please sanitize all PII. If you can provide a one-page statement about retention/residency and a CSV sample (header + 5 rows) that would be ideal. Our compliance team will review and may come back with specific schema mapping questions.

Thanks — Sarah
Sarah Nguyen
Senior Manager, Cloud Security & Compliance
FinCo Bank

Hi Sarah / Jordan — attaching the sanitized sample and a short technical note. Quick summary inline: 

- Attached: audit-log-sample-20260330.csv (CSV, 5 rows, headers as requested) and redwood-audit-logs-spec-20260331.pdf (one-page technical note).
- What we record: timestamp_utc, actor_id (user_id or service principal), api_key_id, request_id, resource_id, operation, source_ip, payload_present. We do not include full request/response payloads in the default audit export unless the customer enables debug logging — that is off by default.
- Retention: Hosted default retention is 365 days. For Dedicated customers we can configure retention up to customer-specified windows; Private (on-prem/VPC) customers control retention per their infrastructure. A 7-year retention is supported in Dedicated or Private deployments; Hosted can be extended via an enterprise contract / add-on (we've included pricing notes in the attached PDF).
- Residency: Hosted logs are stored in the region backing the customer's deployment (e.g., us-east-1). Dedicated and Private can be provisioned in specified regions / on-prem.
- Export formats: CSV and JSON lines supported; exports can be delivered via secure S3 bucket or direct download (sanitized).

Attachments (sanitized):
- audit-log-sample-20260330.csv (CSV, 5 rows)
- redwood-audit-logs-spec-20260331.pdf (technical note: retention/residency/pricing summary)

If you'd like, we can schedule a short sync between FinCo's compliance team and our security product lead to walk through the spec.

Best,
Ben Carter
